pr_title: Sc timer pwm period bug fix
pr_body:
Bug fix for #55284

If a user were to test a pwm signal with the pwm_api test it will succeed, 
however, if they were to change to ordering of the test to allow the nanosecond
test to run before the generic cycles test, the user will notice an inconsistency in
the pwm duty_cycle, this PR address this issue by testing for a change in duty
cycle as well as a change in period length before the driver suggests to create a
new pwm channel.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/55284

issue_context.title: driver: pwm: sctimer: duty_cycle breaks on period length change.
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If the period length of a pwm signal changes, the driver
will assume that a new signal is to be used and creates 
an offset of the original duty cycle by 10% from the 
side effect of calling SCTIMER_SetupPwm for a signal 
that is already setup.

Environment: 
OS; Windows 10
cmake: 3.26.0

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. mkdir build
2. west build -p always -b lpcxpresso55s69_cpu0 zephyr/tests/drivers/pwm/pwm_api
3. west flash

**Expected behavior**
Duty Cycle runs at 50% ->100% -> 0% ->50% ->100% -> 0%

**Impact**
Tests will break if the order is swapped starting at a pwm freq and 
switching the signal to a lower freq due to the way SCTIMER_SetUpPwm
sets up the pwm timers.

review_comments: could you check for pulse cycles here instead and achieve the same effect?
on second glance, I guess period cycles is stored in the data struct but not pulse cycles...
I do not understand why this is needed. Please elaborate a bit.

I am not sure if it is due to the updated ztest framework, or through driver changes, but without this sleep, the pwm signal will drop to 0% duty cycle for only a few milliseconds and jump straight to the next test which in this case is 50% duty cycle.

I think the issue here is that with the new ZTEST framework, the `test_pwm_cycle` test will run, and directly afterwards the `test_pwm_nsec` test will run. Without this delay, the 0% duty cycle signal will only show up for a moment before the PWM signal is reconfigured to 50% duty cycle at the start of `test_pwm_nsec`

@henrikbrixandersen The idea of this test is that the PWM will output signal based on each of the six configurations for one second, and this output can be measured by some kind of signal analyzer to verify functionality. Therefore, before re-configuring the PWM module for the next configuration, the core needs to allow the PWM to operate for one second at each configuration. The mechanism used to accomplish this is a k_sleep(1000), and one of them is missing for one of the configurations, meaning that configuration is essentially skipped, which is a bug.
